_comment: Nightly mutation testing over the pure engine (packages/core). A green unit suite that survives every mutant is not a suite: it pins behaviour nobody asserted. At P0 this reported; at P1 it is a gate, so `thresholds.break` is a number and .github/workflows/mutation.yml no longer carries continue-on-error. The recorded score and the threshold are in docs/P1-REPORT.md — 'the mutation job is green' is not a measurement.
mutate_comment: Every engine module under packages/core/src, and nothing else. The three exclusions are deliberate: *.test.ts is the suite doing the killing; index.ts is a barrel of re-exports whose mutants are all equivalent; journey/** is the phase gate's own harness (it scans the repo and drives a 30-day trace — it is test infrastructure that happens to live in a .ts file, and mutating it measures the gate, not the engine).
thresholds_comment: high/low colour the report. `break` is the gate: below it the run exits non-zero. It is set from a measured baseline (docs/P1-REPORT.md records the number and the date) and is raised, never lowered, when the engine grows a well-tested module. A threshold above the measured score would make the first nightly red for a reason nobody would read.
timeout_comment: A mutant that loops forever must be reported as a timeout rather than hanging the job. The engine's slowest unit tests are the four-zone properties at 10,000 cases per zone (~3.5 s locally, ~2.5x that on ubuntu-latest), so the factor is generous on purpose: a timeout counted as 'killed' is free score.
